context: a letter from J. D. Hooker, which you are answering
exchanges:
I am disgusted at remembering suddenly that I had forgotten to send the vols: of DC.— I shall send on Thursday by carrier that with Leguminosæ (& others)—for I am really interested in that curious anomaly.

Bentham I know thinks that he has created too many genera & others far more.—but whether enough to influence the whole Flora is more than I can tell—

I have begun my Introd: Essay to Tasmania Flora. I think I shall confine it to a clear exposition of all the main features of the Flora of Australia & leave all conclusion drawing to others. I find there are already upwards of 100 Europ. plants well naturalize⁠⟨⁠d⁠⟩⁠ in vicinity of Melbourne already.

I send by post 2 tracts from A Gray— I cannot follow Dana’s metaphysical ideas on species. What do you say to them

Ever yours | J D Hooker

The Books arrived quite safely this morning.

I will do D. Candolle first, as I guess that most likely to be wanted: the job will be a long one.—

Whenever I try the Labiatæ in different ways, which will not be soon, you shall hear the result, as I shall wish much to tell it.

Thanks for Dana’s pamphlet: I am much disappointed in it. I have high respect for Dana, but in this brochure “I do not think he is much of a Baconian philosopher,” as our friend J. E. Gray says.— I hate such far-fetched analogies, as comparing an atom of oxygen with a living being.— I believe, poor fellow, he believes in 1st Chr. of Genesis, so great allowances must be made for him.

I am very sorry to hear that you do not intend to give generalisations in your Tasmanian Introduction, but I do not believe you will be able to resist: what is in the spirit must come out.
